Definition: Beth-Nimrah, a place east of the Jordan
BiblicalUsage: Beth-Nimrah means house of the leopard, and it is named twice, both times as a town of Gad east of the Jordan. Numbers 32:36 lists it among the fenced cities the Gadites built, with folds for sheep, and Joshua 13:27 sets it in the valley, in the rest of the kingdom of Sihon. A walled town with a wild name.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that a town named for a leopard, built with sheepfolds, is a good picture of Israel east of the Jordan: walled, watchful, and settled.
